name: ambiguous
title: Ambiguous: 'make it more robust and safer, with better insight into who is clicking'

baseline.hint: Run the greenfield and brownfield scenarios against the same --target first.

impl:T1.rationale: Limits on and forwarded headers untrusted by default, so an unconfigured deployment is the safe one.

impl:T2.rationale: Token bucket with continuous refill and a hard cap on tracked clients; time is injected so behaviour is tested without sleeping.

impl:T3.rationale: Pure function over the parsed URL; numeric-looking hosts must parse as a plain public address so alternative IP spellings cannot slip through.

impl:T4.rationale: Visitor identifiers are an HMAC under a memory-only key that rotates daily; the schema only ever sees an opaque value.

impl:T5.rationale: Limits are route dependencies, vetting is part of URL validation, and the redirect path hands only derived, non-identifying values to storage.

documentation.rationale: README documents limits, destination rules, the privacy model and the single-instance caveats; changelog flags the referrer behaviour change.

approvals.comment: Answers below. Keep it to code changes we can ship this sprint.

answers.Q1: Rate-limit each client. Creation is the abuse vector; give redirects a much looser limit. No caching or scale-out now.
answers.Q2: Rule-based blocking plus a configurable blocklist. No external reputation service this quarter.
answers.Q3: Aggregates only: unique visitors and top referrers. We must not store IP addresses, user agents or location.

approvals.comment: Two blockers. (1) ADR-14: SHA-256 of an IP address is not anonymous - the IPv4 space can be enumerated, so this is still personal data and contradicts the product owner's answer to Q3. Use a keyed hash with a key that lives only in memory and rotates daily. (2) ADR-12: trusting X-Forwarded-For unconditionally lets any client pick its own identity and walk around the limiter. Trust it only when a proxy is explicitly configured, and then only the entry the proxy appended.
Both points addressed in ADR-12 and ADR-14; plan updated accordingly. Approved.
Migration 3 adds one nullable column holding an opaque value. Approved to run.
Checklist green; privacy test confirms nothing identifying is stored. Promote.
